title: Drummers and the Casino Gardens job
summary: Earl Carter fills in for Sbarbaro, and Harry James offers $75 a week at Casino Gardens.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What was his name again? Carter?

Earl Carter. Yeah. A Chicago drummer. He filled in for two weeks. And Spobara comes up and takes his place. This man knew that that's all the way we used him for two weeks. And we did pretty good at the Del Abbey. Then Harry James buys an entrance in the Casino Gardens with Aikenbar and Reeves. And he approaches us and offers us $75 a week to play in the Casino Gardens. We went and played the Casino Gardens. That was Kinzen Clock. And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself. Well, this man on the Clarence, he liked to drink, mix with the people. And you can't go anywhere doing that, mixing with the patrons of the place, drinking with them, sitting at the table. And every time he'd want them to put you in a mind of some bordello, you'd have to give them a signal for them to come and play. So I got mad at him. And I had heard from Shields. And I had sent Shields money to come to Chicago. Then I give this man his two weeks' notice. That was about the second or third week that we played at the Shields Cafe. We started there around... Could have been in August, somewhere in August. I'm not sure the exact date. stuff like stuff
